Figure 10: The average growth rate on the reaction surface of the boule visualized as all unique combinations of 2D projections from the 8D parameter space. Yellow values indicate higher growth rate. As seen in Figure 10, there are clear trends along certain directions of the parameter space. For example, when examining the effect of reactor pressure (left-hand column) it is evident that higher operating pressures are typically associated with higher average growth rates. Similarly, the reaction channel or “chamber” height seems to be strongly correlated with average growth rate, where narrower channels lead to higher growth rates. Other relationships are less clear, for example, increasing the argon inflow rate is associated with both very low or very high growth rate depending on the operating pressure of the reactor, and the effect of boule-wall gap seems at least somewhat correlated with the chamber height. We will proceed with a more quantitative evaluation of these sensitivities shortly, but first, present the corresponding 2D projections for the constraint on maximum molar fraction of TCS near the neck region, since optimizing growth rate alone is not sufficient if the optimal design generates a high degree of invasion and fouling of TCS near the neck. The effect of these randomized designs and operating conditions on TCS is shown in Figure 11.
